question: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$. Check whether $f$ is onto. Give mathematical justification.
explanation:
Range restriction
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, we have $x^2\geq0$. Therefore,
$$f(x)=x^2+1\geq1.$$
Thus, the range of $f$ is $[1,\infty)$, which is not equal to the co-domain $\mathbb{R}$.

Element without a pre-image
The number $0\in\mathbb{R}$ belongs to the co-domain, but there is no real $x$ satisfying
$$x^2+1=0,$$
because this would require $x^2=-1$.

Conclusion
Since at least one element of the co-domain has no pre-image, $f$ is not onto.

options.A: $f$ is not onto because its range is $[1,\infty)$, so $0$ has no real pre-image
options.B: $f$ is onto because every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ has the pre-image $x=\sqrt{y-1}$
options.C: $f$ is not onto because $1$ has no real pre-image
options.D: $f$ is onto because $x^2+1$ is real for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$
